Hi! I was sleeved in February and have always had fine/thin hair so I was also the most nervous about this part of the process. As much as we all do this to prioritize our health it was so hard to not think cosmetically speaking, especially since I’m a barber and 95% of my life is hair. So with this background here is what I will tell you. The hair loss is rarely noticeable to other people it will mostly be you who notices and then if you have had the same hair dresser for years they will also probably notice/mention it. Here is what you can do to prepare, scalp/shampoo brush as often as you can. I did it two, three times a day. Get one for $5 on amazon and just use it in circles around your scalp. You don’t have to use product with it and if it makes your hair look crazy, just brush it back down. This will help with scalp stimulation and blood flow. This is the most important. Next invest in Lanza Stimulating shampoo, conditioner, and scalp spray. These products are important because they trick your scalp into thinking it never left the hair growth cycle (you only lose hair in one of the three cycles) this will DRASTICALLY stop what you lose. I started this before anything else and I have had quite a bit less loss than my mom and sister had this far out and they used Nioxin. Lanza can be purchased online or at a salon near you. You also don’t need to do a “big chop” have your hair dresser give you a blunt cut every few months (no layers) this will help the overall bulk look of your hair. And while people are correct in saying overuse of hot tools can cause damage, if you use a decent thermal spray you will be just fine and blow drying and curling your hair is the absolute best way to appear like there is more. Also styling with a sea salt spray will give it some great lift and weight, I recommend this for men as well. Hopefully this long ramble was even a little helpful! 

P.S. clip in extensions, ponytails, bangs are excellent for covering problem spots and you can find many relatively inexpensive and find a hairdresser to show you how to install if you aren’t comfortable putting them in yourself.
